bottom_line: In patients with severe heart failure, dronedarone vs placebo increased all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.07 to 4.25).
implications: These data support that, in this severe heart failure population, dronedarone increased early all-cause mortality versus placebo (8.1% vs 3.8%; hazard ratio, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.07 to 4.25), while the primary composite endpoint was not statistically different (17.1% vs 12.6%; hazard ratio, 1.38; 95% CI, 0.92 to 2.09). The trial’s early termination and small number of deaths limit conclusions about other endpoints beyond the reported estimates.

major_points.text: Planned as a multicenter, double-blind randomized trial comparing dronedarone 400 mg twice daily vs placebo in hospitalized symptomatic HF with severe LV systolic dysfunction.
major_points.quote: In a multicenter study with a double-blind design, we planned to randomly assign 1000 patients who were hospitalized with symptomatic heart failure and severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction to receive 400 mg of dronedarone twice a day or placebo.

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early for safety after 627 patients were included, per DSMB recommendation and prespecified stopping rule.
major_points.quote: After inclusion of 627 patients (310 in the dronedarone group and 317 in the placebo group), the trial was prematurely terminated for safety reasons, at the recommendation of the data and safety monitoring board

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was higher with dronedarone during the randomized study period.
major_points.quote: 25 patients in the dronedarone group (8.1%) and 12 patients in the placebo group (3.8%) died (hazard ratio in the dronedarone group, 2.13; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07 to 4.25; P = 0.03).

major_points.text: Primary composite endpoint (death from any cause or hospitalization for worsening heart failure) was not significantly different between groups.
major_points.quote: there were 53 events in the dronedarone group (17.1%) and 40 events in the placebo group (12.6%) (hazard ratio, 1.38; 95% CI, 0.92 to 2.09; P = 0.12).

major_points.text: Creatinine increases as serious adverse events occurred more often with dronedarone.
major_points.quote: More increases in the creatinine concentration were reported as serious adverse events in the dronedarone group than in the placebo group.

subgroups.text: After the trial was stopped, steering committee decided to perform post hoc subgroup analyses of mortality for eight variables.
subgroups.quote: after the trial was stopped, the steering committee decided to per­form post hoc subgroup analyses of the mortality end point for eight variables.

subgroups.text: Subgroup analysis by baseline estimated GFR showed hazard ratio for death 3.32 for <50 vs 0.89 for ≥50 (P value for interaction 0.09).

No cases of torsades de pointes were observed in either group.
harms.quote: No cases of torsades de pointes were observed in either group.

harms.text: Mean estimated GFR was 7 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 lower in dronedarone group than placebo group (P = 0.009) and returned to baseline after termination.
harms.quote: The mean estimated glomer­ular filtration rate was 7 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area lower in the dronedarone group than in the placebo group (P = 0.009).

analysis_methods.text: Sample size based on expected 50% event rate in placebo, 20% relative reduction, two-sided type 2 error 5%, power 90%.

analysis_methods.text: Times to events analyzed with two-sided log-rank test; Kaplan–Meier used for life-table plots.
